chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Magi man, or a polytheist from other than the People of the Book, under whom is a wife, so he becomes a Muslim, or she becomes a Muslim. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should await with that the expiration of her waiting period, and if he has become a Muslim, or she has become a Muslim before the expiration of her waiting period, so they are both upon their first marriage; and if he does not become a Muslim until after the expiration of the waiting period, so she is irrevocably divorced from him'.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage of a non-Muslim man and Muslim woman if one converts to Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of 'temporary' marriages between Ahl al-Kitab or polytheists and Muslims upon conversion, a key issue in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of existing unions. It establishes that if one spouse converts before the other's waiting period (iddah) expires, the original marriage contract remains intact; however, if the waiting period elapses before conversion, the marriage is automatically dissolved (talaq ba'in). This ruling underscores the principle that religious disparity invalidates the marital bond, necessitating a new contract or separation.
